governanceNotes: D1 batch 39 (2026-09-23): deferred. Negative screen recorded 2026-09-23: (i) direction is inverted for outcome purposes - the Kezirian 2021 JAMA Dermatology matched-cohort study of 5,148 granuloma annulare patients documents baseline type 2 diabetes in 21.1% versus 13.3% of matched controls (adjusted OR 1.24) and incident diabetes also elevated (adjusted OR 1.31), with rheumatoid arthritis likewise enriched at baseline and incident follow-up (adjusted OR 2.05), and its own conclusion states that diabetes and hyperlipidemia may be risk factors for the development of granuloma annulare with autoimmunity an important factor in pathogenesis - i.e., the metabolic and autoimmune drivers run TOWARD granuloma annulare, not from it; the Kadlec 2026 JAAD update review documents the disease-association landscape (hyperlipidemia, diabetes mellitus, thyroiditis, rheumatoid arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus) in the same upstream-driver framing, and the Murphree 2021 review and Fukami 2020 interstitial-granuloma-annulare review document the metabolic, infectious, and autoimmune association pattern with pathogenesis discussion rather than downstream outcome cohorts; (ii) zero-record outcome screening - no record quantifies granuloma-annulare-attributable downstream outcomes (the lesions are self-limited with spontaneous resolution in most patients and recurrence, not systemic progression, is what the literature documents); (iii) wrong-direction guard - authoring granuloma-annulare-to-diabetes-mellitus or granuloma-annulare-to-rheumatoid-arthritis would assert arrows the anchor study contradicts while diabetes-mellitus and rheumatoid-arthritis exist as catalog identities whose OWN windows are the correct venue for the driver-to-skin direction (diabetes-mellitus is a zero-edge backlog identity; rheumatoid-arthritis is published with its own outgoing edges); (iv) the localized-versus-generalized distinction is not cataloged, so generalized-disease outcomes cannot be scoped. Reopening condition: a longitudinal cohort with granuloma annulare onset documented before a catalog-fit outcome with metabolic and autoimmune confounders controlled, or a granuloma-annulare-specific systemic-complication series.
